run: a blind pronunciation review of the A/B/C renders: which Persian words OmniVoice gets wrong, and whether diacritics or IPA input fix them
status: complete 2026-10-03: one listener (the user) answered all 14 sentences; read through the key the same day
why: the user deferred the voice listening test until pronunciation is fixed. [measured] on the sealed Neyshekar set the recogniser reads the speakers' own recordings at CER 6.4% and OmniVoice's renders at 9.9%. Before fixing, the errors have to be found: this asks a native listener to mark them word by word

material.renders: eval/runs/omnivoice-ipa-ab-v3 (2026-09-24): 14 hard sentences - homographs (gol/gel, mard/mord, ruye), an ezafe chain, difficult consonants, clusters, colloquial, long, four of the sealed test texts and a corpus sentence - in the voice of the Mana-TTS reference

conditions.A: OmniVoice on plain Persian script (what the app does)
conditions.B: OmniVoice on a diacritised twin (11 sentences; none written for the 3 long ones)
conditions.C: the OmniVoice IPA fine-tune on canonical IPA from Homo-GE2PE, which read the twin where one exists

wrong_in_twins_found_before_listening.t11: بارانِ بَند آمد: no ezafe on باران (the rain stopped)
wrong_in_twins_found_before_listening.s08: حِرفا should be حَرفا; خُریدار should be خَریدار

blind: per sentence the renders take slots 1-3 in balanced orders (each condition in each slot about equally often, seed 20261004) under anonymous file names; all renders of a sentence matched to one loudness by gain; the page shows only the plain sentence, never a twin. The key is eval/runs/evidence/pronunciation-review-v1/key.json (fingerprint fdc17ebfc261c9e6)
asked_per_render: either 'every word right' or the words said wrong (tapped on the sentence's words), with an optional note of what was heard
asked_per_sentence: which render read best (or no difference)

analysis_fixed_before_listening.per_condition: renders with no marked word out of those answered; words marked wrong out of the words in those renders; times picked as reading best
analysis_fixed_before_listening.also: the same by sentence category, and every marked word with the listener's note; a mark under B or C on a sentence whose twin is wrong is listed with that note
analysis_fixed_before_listening.what_it_is_for: deciding the fix: if B or C clears what A gets wrong, the input form is the lever (diacritics or phonemes before the model); if all three fail on the same words, it is the model or the twins; the categories say which kinds of words
analysis_fixed_before_listening.not_claimed: fourteen sentences, one voice, one seed and few listeners: a diagnostic, not a measure of any system's pronunciation

delivery: one private page, https://claude.ai/artifact/8t3wc2esQ1TCdRZ5wFAQCU (published 2026-10-03, source eval/runs/evidence/pronunciation-review-v1/page.html): one sentence per screen in the key's order, the plain sentence on top, each reading with its own player, the sentence's words to tap when said wrong, an 'every word right' button and an optional note; then which reading was best. It names no condition. Answers are kept in its database as reviews/<listener id> (the owner reads all, each listener only their own) or, for anyone who cannot write there, as an answer code to send
checked_before_listening: 2026-10-03: 39 audio files and the page on the artifact; a probe record written as the owner was readable by the owner, hidden at a listener's level, then deleted

result.listener: one: the user, a native speaker who also runs this project - blind to which reading was which, not to what the review was for

what_A_gets_wrong.classified_by: Claude, from the words marked and the listener's notes; the notes are in answers-listener-1.json
ezafe_missing_where_it_belongs: باران (s06, read with a pause instead)
other: بود with a vowel after it (s09)
what_A_gets_wrong.summary: 9 of the 19 errors are ezafe - 5 added, 4 missing - and 8 are short vowels, two of them homographs

what_B_shows.the_model_reads_the_marks: where a twin's marks were right, B cleared errors A made in the same sentence: chatr and the ezafe of باران (s06 read without error), the ezafe of خوب (s03 without error), قلعه (s05). Where a twin's marks were wrong it read them as written: حِرفا and خُریدار (s08), اِمانت (t10), the ezafe of بارانِ (t11) - all four marked wrong, in sentences A read right or wrong the same way
what_B_shows.marks_it_misreads: a damma came out as a long u twice: گُل as gul (s01), کُشتی as kushti (t09)
what_B_shows.what_marks_did_not_fix: ezafe added where the twin left a word unmarked (دانشگاه s07, غروب s05) and ezafe missing where the twin missed it too (پایان t09)
what_B_shows.disputed: پیرمرد was marked wrong for pirmard where the listener expected pir-e mard; dictionaries give pirmard

result.what_C_shows: the IPA model is worst on every count - no reading without an error, 13.6% of words, never picked best - and the listener's notes say its accent sounds foreign even where the words are right. The route is closed
result.reading: the errors are mostly about what the plain script leaves out - ezafe and short vowels - and OmniVoice follows explicit marks when it is given them, right or wrong. So the lever is the text front-end: write ezafe and the needed short vowels into the input, from a source accurate enough that its marks are right, and mark where no ezafe belongs. The damma misreads say to mark only what a word needs. Phonemes through the IPA model are not the way
result.not_claimed: one listener, fourteen sentences, one voice and one seed, and the sentences were chosen to be hard: a diagnostic of error types, not a measure of any system's pronunciation. These sentences are now development material; a fix is measured on new ones written before it

erratum_2026_10_03: result.what_B_shows.disputed says dictionaries give پیرمرد as pirmard. That was written from memory, not looked up. KaamelDict, checked 2026-10-03, gives piremard - the listener's reading - so B's mark on پیرمرد is an error like the others, not a dispute
